answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to escrow a bond before receiving high-value jobs, then randomly audit signed work and slash the bond when a verifier proves fraud. A hundred names do not create a hundred free chances: each must lock real capital, and attacks risk losing it. This makes Sybil influence costly, not impossible; at the nadir of trust, buyers can begin with small jobs rather than rely on a fable of perfect identity. Reputation maps paths across a mesa, but the bond supplies the barrier.
